title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Confidentiality vs Privilege
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: What is the key difference between a paralegal's duty of confidentiality and solicitor-client (paralegal-client) privilege?
options: There is no difference; the terms mean exactly the same thing in Ontario law.
Confidentiality applies only to financial records, while privilege applies to all communication.

Confidentiality is an ethical duty covering all information acquired in the course of the professional relationship, whereas privilege is an evidentiary rule protecting specific legal communications from disclosure in court.
Privilege is owed to the court, while confidentiality is owed to the client.
questions.explain: Confidentiality is a broad ethical obligation (Rule 3.03) that applies to *all* information concerning the business and affairs of a client acquired in the course of the professional relationship. Privilege is a narrower evidentiary rule that protects communications made in confidence between a legal representative and client for the purpose of seeking or giving legal advice from being compelled in court.
